instructions: Rinse the 1.5 cups rice in a few changes of water until the water runs mostly clear. Cook it in a rice cooker, or in a covered pot with 1 3/4 cups water over low heat for 18 minutes, then leave it covered off the heat for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, drain the tofu and pat it dry. Cut each block across into 8 slices about 1/2 inch thick. Lay them on paper towels and press the tops dry with more towels.

In a small bowl, stir together 1/4 cup soy sauce, 1/4 cup water, the 2 tbsp sesame oil, 2 tsp brown sugar, the 2 tsp sesame seeds and 1 tsp of the gochugaru. Mince the 2 garlic cloves into the bowl and stir again.
Put the other 1 tsp gochugaru in a small bowl for the table. Thinly slice 4 of the scallions.

Heat 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium. Add half the tofu in one layer and cook it for about 4 minutes, until the underside is golden. Flip the slices and cook the other side for 4 minutes. Transfer them to a plate.
Add the last 1 tbsp vegetable oil and brown the rest of the tofu the same way.
Put all the tofu back in the pan, overlapping a little if you need to, and turn the heat to low. Pour the sauce over it, lifting a few slices so it runs underneath.
Simmer for 10 minutes, until the sauce has cooked down to a glaze that clings to the tofu. Flip the slices halfway through and spoon the sauce over them.
Taste a piece. If it's flat, add a splash more soy sauce.
Scatter the scallions over the top. Serve with the rice, with the gochugaru on the side.
method_notes: Every version cuts firm tofu into 1/2 inch slabs, browns them in a little oil, then simmers them in a soy, sesame oil, sugar, garlic, sesame seed and gochugaru sauce with scallions, served with rice. Tasting Table browns for 4 minutes a side and simmers on low for 10 minutes with a no-water soy sauce; Korean Bapsang cuts the soy with an equal amount of water and simmers only about 5 minutes; Beyond Kimchee adds onion, anchovy stock and more gochugaru. This one follows Tasting Table's method doubled to two blocks for a dinner for four, uses Korean Bapsang's equal water so the doubled soy isn't too salty, and splits the gochugaru between the pan and the table.
